用 ruststream-sqlx 在 RustStream 服务中使用 SQL 数据库的指南：服务自有表中的任务队列，以及事务性 outbox。
SQL 表中的队列如何工作，ruststream-sqlx 在数据库与 RustStream 运行时之间处于什么位置，以及这样做的开销。
ruststream-sqlx 在每条消息上的开销：与裸 sqlx 循环对照的吞吐量，作为插件的 outbox，以及它自身代码的指令数和内存分配次数。
ruststream-sqlx 如何测量自己：三个循环、在真实数据库上的运行、受数据库限制的判定计算、吞吐量网格和代码计数。
ruststream-sqlx 的基准测试数字测量什么，一条消息仍然要付出什么，以及这些数字不能用来得出什么结论。
ruststream-sqlx 的位置：在 RustStream 运行时与服务的 sqlx 连接池之间，SQL 为每个订阅构建一次，outbox 可以与任意 Broker 配合。
一个订阅为每个空闲 worker 保持一次进行中的领取，上限是连接池大小减一；workers_by_key(n) 让每个分区键留在一个工作分区上。
SqlxBroker::new 记录配置，connect 确定方言，每个订阅在启动时预备自己的 SQL，shutdown 停止领取。
outbox 在任意 Broker 上把每次发布记录到服务自己的表中，消费者确认后标记记录，并在启动时重发其余记录。
一行在服务中的路径：领取、投递、解码、处理器、应答和结算，可以逐行处理、按批处理，或者以行本身交给处理器。
队列就是服务自己的一张表：一行是一条消息，一个组是一个队列，各列的角色决定一行何时到期，以及结果做什么。
领取一行的三种方式：由打开的事务持有的行锁、写入行中的租约，以及键上的咨询锁，各以连接数计价。
本 crate 为一次投递打开的事务：行锁方式的领取事务，以及在事务模式下处理器写入所用、按表的隔离级别打开的事务。
订阅在领取总是取满时持续领取，否则等待它的轮询间隔，同一 Broker 的发布或一条通知会提前结束这次等待。
在每种领取方式下，ack、drop、retry 和 retry_after 向队列表写入什么，以及尝试计数和死信如何把一次重试变成一次转移。
ruststream-sqlx serves task queues in the service's own SQL tables and tracks what a service publishes on any broker in an outbox.
With asyncapi the document names the database server and, on each subscription's channel, the table it reads and its group; rows get their schema.
Each InboxQueue channel carries x-sqlx: the table it reads, qualified with its schema, and the group its name selects where the table has groups.
The server is the pool's host and port with the protocol postgres or mysql, SQLite in process with no host, an AnyPool by its scheme, never a credential.
SqlxBroker serves the queues in the tables of the service's sqlx pool; new records the pool, and connect checks one connection and picks the dialect.
Each message in work holds pool connections by its form; workers(n) claims in parallel but always leaves the pool one connection for handlers.
SqlxBrokerError is the inbox's one error type: connecting, statements, the schema, declarations, leases, transactions, publishes, and a closed broker.
One glob, ruststream_sqlx::prelude, brings the core prelude, the derives, the broker, InboxQueue, its steps, the publish policies and the keys.
Shutdown returns ClosedSqlxBroker, releases every advisory lock in work, and a publisher kept past it reports SqlxBrokerError::Closed.
A subscription builds and prepares its statements when it opens, so a missing table or column, a retry the table cannot carry or a second reader stops startup.
A handler reads the inbox's context through Ctx<keys::..>: the transaction, the pool and the attempt, in that order, leaving out what it does not need.
keys::Attempt reads the delivery's attempt, 1 for the first: the attempt column as it stood before the claim, None where the table has none.
keys::Pool gives a handler the service's pool, whose writes commit on their own whatever the outcome; on dedicated threads it is the thread's pool.
SqlxBroker::new takes the dialect built in for its pool's database; statements are built once when a subscription opens, the insert at compile time.
With any, an AnyPool is served by the built-in dialect of the database it reaches at connect; its rows hold integers, text and bytes only.
SqlxBroker::with_dialect serves a database with a dialect of the service's own: Dialect, then the trait of each form it builds, and ByName for names.
mysql serves MySQL 8.0.1 and MariaDB 10.6 or later in every form, READ COMMITTED by default; index the claim order so a claim reads its own group.
On Postgres every form runs: SKIP LOCKED claims, a one-statement lease claim, advisory locks on 64-bit hashes, statement_timestamp and LISTEN/NOTIFY.
sqlite serves the lease and advisory lock forms in the service's process: one writer at a time, times as text, and no server to run in tests.
A table takes rows by row lock unless it names another form: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED in a transaction held while the handler runs.
advisory_lock = ".." holds each row by a lock on its key: rows that share a key go into work one at a time, and a crashed session frees its rows.
#[field(locked_until)] selects the lease form: the claim writes an expiry and commits, the handler holds no connection, and the lease is extended.
custom(lock, unlock) hands the lock and the release of each key to the service's SQL, so a queue shares a lock another system already takes.
A headers column keeps a delivery's headers as a JSON object of strings; a publish with a header the column cannot hold is refused.
custom(fetch) reads the claimed rows with the service's own SELECT, such as a join; a claimed id it returns no row for settles by the decode policy.
HeaderColumn lets a headers column hold a type of the service's own; it moves the map in and out and names a header it cannot keep byte for byte.
Each field of a headers struct without a role is a header: strings and bytes as they are, numbers in decimal, times in RFC 3339, None left out.
In the headers layout a headers struct describes the queue table and its header fields, and the message struct that flattens it is what a handler takes.
A table with a payload column is in payload mode: the claim lends the column's bytes to the codec, and the handler takes the decoded message.
A claimed row that does not decode is settled by the subscription's decode policy before the handler runs, and still spends its attempt.
A table without a payload column is in row mode: a handler takes the struct itself as the driver read it, one row or a slice per claim.
The outbox records each message a service publishes under a registered name until a consumer processed it, and publishes the rest again at startup.
The outbox wraps inbox handlers as any other; a record written from a transactional handler commits on its own, whatever the delivery's outcome.
OutboxError names what the outbox could not do: record a publish, read the unprocessed records, or republish one, and a publish with no pool yet.
#[derive(Outbox)] describes the outbox table: id, name and payload are required, headers and processed_at optional; the service writes the record.
outbox! registers record types under the names they track and returns the registry; a name written twice does not compile.
b.after_startup(policy, tracking.republish()) sends every unprocessed record again once the subscriptions are open; republish_names picks names.
Inside #[ruststream::app] the registry starts without a pool, and on_startup builds one and hands it over with set_pool; the service closes it.
custom(fetch, ack, retry, discard, recover) replaces a record's default statement with the service's own, for a status of its own or a saga.
A test build leaves the outbox off, so a test needs no outbox table; RUSTSTREAM_SQLX_OUTBOX=on turns it on for the whole test process.
Outbox::layer and publish_layer track messages: the publish records then sends, and the delivery's outcome settles its record by its id.
Outbox::wrap gives a publisher outside the publish pipeline the same tracking, for an HTTP endpoint or an after_startup hook.
A publish writes a row through the row's Publish, the service's own INSERT; Repository names the table at compile time, a static call per publish.
SqlxBroker::route leads a name into a row type's table in both directions; Routed, the default for replies and slots, looks each name up.
A handler's outcome is a statement on its row: ack deletes it or sets processed_at, retry returns it at once with one more attempt, drop finishes it.
max_attempts(n) with dead_letter(..) moves a row whose attempts are spent into another group, or into a table with the same columns.
retry_after(d) hides the row until its retry_after column comes due; a table without the column returns the row at once and logs a warning.
InboxQueue reads one queue of a table: its name selects a group where the table has a group column and addresses the whole table where it has none.
A slice handler gets one claim of up to batch(n) rows; each row settles on its own, and in the row lock form the settlements commit together.
#[field(group, fifo = true)] keeps each group in order: one row of a group in work at a time across every broker, the head first.
A subscription by name, #[subscriber("emails")], reads the table its route leads to; it takes the broker's settings and no retry cap.
on_threads runs an InboxQueue subscription's handlers on dedicated threads, each with a pool of its own, counted against connection_limit.
A subscription claims while its claims come back full, then waits the poll interval, one second unless the broker or the queue sets another.
workers(n) keeps a claim in flight for each free worker, bounded by the pool; with a partition_key column workers_by_key(n) keeps each key in order.
#[derive(Inbox)] describes a queue table with an ordinary sqlx struct: the table in #[inbox(..)], column roles in #[field(..)], names from sqlx.
#[inbox(checked, db = ..)] puts the statements a struct determines into sqlx's compile-time check against DATABASE_URL or the .sqlx offline data.
A column is named in one place, sqlx's attributes: rename, rename_all, raw identifiers and skip; a flattened field makes statements select every column.
custom(..) hands one event of a table to the service's own SQL, Claim to Extend, and every other event keeps the statement the dialect builds.
A table described by hand implements InboxTable: a const InboxSpec chain, its settings as types in type Table, and the same statements as the derive.
Insert writes a task with the derive's generated insert, inside the service's own transaction, so the task commits with the data it serves.
Each #[field(..)] role turns on one behaviour of the queue: group, priority, partition key, retry_after, attempt, processed_at, lease, headers, payload.
TestApp::start runs the service against a real database, SQLite in memory for a start, with the harness waiting on every publish and a pausable clock.
TestApp::start_live runs the same test body on the real clock, against a database of the test's own on Postgres, MySQL or MariaDB.
A queue reads "now" to claim, delay and mark rows; by default the host's SystemClock, bound in the column's own type as the service's inserts do.
A clock of the service's own implements Clock and takes the place of SystemClock in clock = .. or .clock::<..>(), for every statement that reads now.
clock = DatabaseClock makes the statements read the database's clock, so every host serving one table reads one clock; the lease form keeps the host's.
A time column holds chrono::DateTime<Utc> or time::OffsetDateTime; SQLite compares times as text, exact for chrono and to the second for time.
.transactional() lends the handler its delivery's transaction: acknowledgement commits the handler's writes with the row's settlement, or neither.
isolation = <level> opens a table's transactions at an isolation level, mode = <mode> at a SQLite mode; a level the dialect does not open does not compile.
A publish through the broker wakes the subscriptions of its table and group in the same process at once; a row written by other means waits the poll.
On Postgres, listen_notify wakes subscriptions on pg_notify from any process: each publish announces its row, and a trigger can announce others.

documents.t: ruststream-sqlx 通过 sqlx 把 SQL 数据库接入 RustStream 服务。它由两部分组成。inbox 是服务自有表中的任务队列，由一个 RustStream Broker 提供服务。outbox 记录服务通过任意 RustStream Broker 发布的每条消息，直到消费者处理完它。两部分都支持 Postgres、MySQL 与 MariaDB，以及 SQLite。指南带着一个服务从 SQLite 上的第一个队列出发，经过重试、顺序、事务和多个实例，走到 Postgres 上的生产环境，并跟踪它在其他 Broker 上发布的内容。从快速开始读起。
本节用图说明 SQL 表中的队列如何工作，ruststream-sqlx 在数据库与 RustStream 运行时之间处于什么位置，以及这给服务带来的开销。
ruststream-sqlx 在每条消息上的开销：与裸 sqlx 循环对照的吞吐量，作为插件的 outbox，以及它自身代码的指令数和内存分配次数。

第一张图在测试环境的 PostgreSQL 上把每个场景用三种方式运行。裸 sqlx 循环 是手写的循环，它在以同样方式构建的连接池上，按同样的顺序执行 Broker 对同一张表执行的那些语句；这些语句取自方言，因此两者不会走样。手动驱动 crate 用一个自己的循环驱动本 crate 的订阅或发布者，没有运行时。RustStream 服务 是用户写的服务：一张 #[derive(Inbox)] 表、一个 #[subscriber] 处理器和应用。第一项差值是本 crate 在它所执行的语句之外的开销，第二项是运行时在其上增加的开销。 每个循环画成一条横条，从最佳一轮延伸到最慢的一轮，圆点标出最佳一轮，缺口标出中位一轮。坐标轴的零点是裸循环的最佳一轮，圆点在零点右侧表示更慢。空心圆点表示该循环与裸循环的差异小于各轮的波动范围。图表下方的表格列出最佳一轮，括号里是中位数。 每条消息至少要付出一次领取、一次结算和一次提交，每一项都是一次到数据库的往返。标为 受数据库限制 的行，其裸循环在每条消息上至少有一半时间在等待这些往返。这时本 crate 和运行时的工作发生在裸循环同样要付出的等待之内，该行给出的是它们开销的下限，而不是对开销的测量。
documents.s: 与裸 sqlx 循环对照

documents.t: outbox 可以与任意 Broker 配合，所以把它作为普通应用的一项开销来测量：同一个应用的三个变体，经 ruststream-fred 运行在测试环境的 Redis Pub/Sub 和 PostgreSQL 上。不用 outbox 是用户不使用 outbox 时写的应用。手写的 outbox 是同一个应用，在每次发布前插入记录，再在处理器中取出并标记记录，用裸 sqlx 实现。crate 自带的 outbox 是同一个应用，使用本 crate 的注册表、两个中间件层和重发。与不用 outbox 对照，图表显示跟踪一条消息本身的开销；与手写的 outbox 对照，它显示本 crate 的机制在用户无论如何都会执行的语句之外增加了多少。

开销图统计一条消息在服务线程上的开销：稳态下 callgrind 测得的指令数和 DHAT 测得的内存分配次数，连接测试环境的 PostgreSQL。计数包括运行时、本 crate，以及 sqlx 驱动程序在该线程上的编码和解码；数据库服务器是另一个进程，不计入。冷启动 是启动服务一次性付出的开销：打开连接池的连接、Broker 的启动检查和第一次投递。outbox 的计数让同样的应用运行在 MemoryBroker 上，因此其中不含任何传输的开销。

在每种数据库上，用一个以 workers(n) 挂载的订阅排空一张已填满的表，连接池有 16 个连接，分别使用逐条投递和每批 64 条。PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 采用行锁方式。SQLite 没有行锁，因此采用租约方式。裸循环在一个连接池上运行 n 个任务，每个任务领取、读取并删除，直到领取返回空。本 crate 的循环在同一个连接池上运行 n 个订阅，每个订阅使用自己的 Broker。服务运行一个订阅，由它为所有 worker 领取。outbox 的单元格在 outbox 的三个变体中，都以 workers(n) 挂载中继和接收端。 Postgres，行锁方式各循环比裸循环最佳一轮低多少 裸 sqlx 循环 手动驱动 crate RustStream 服务 各轮，从最佳到最慢 最佳一轮 中位一轮 轮次的波动范围 无法区分 ruststream-sqlx 0.7.0 ruststream-sqlx 如何测量自己：三个循环、在真实数据库上的运行、受数据库限制的判定计算、吞吐量网格和代码计数。流程就是框架自己的流程（RustStream 方法论），本页说明它在 SQL 数据库上是什么样子。

一个进程把每个场景跑三遍，作为三个循环，它们只有一处不同：承载消息的是什么。 裸 sqlx 循环。 直接驱动 sqlx：一个循环在以同样方式构建的连接池上，按同样的顺序执行 Broker 对同一张表执行的那些语句。它的语句取自 Broker 渲染语句所用的方言，因此两个循环执行相同的 SQL。 手动驱动 crate。 本 crate，上面什么也没有：Broker 建立连接，InboxQueue 打开一个订阅，一个循环从它的流中取出投递，逐个解码、读取一个字段并确认；或者把 Repository 和 Routed 配对成发布者。没有处理器，没有应用，也没有分发。 RustStream 服务。 用户写的服务：一张 #[derive(Inbox)] 表、一个 #[subscriber] 处理器，以及 RustStream::new(..).with_broker(SqlxBroker::new(pool), ..)。 其余一切在三个循环中都相同：表、行、解码成的同一个小结构体、四个连接的连接池、带四个工作线程的 tokio 运行时，以及二进制程序。应答场景通过已连接 Broker 的默认发布者 Routed，把每次投递的应答写入第二张表。 outbox 的场景是同一个应用的三个变体，分别占据这三个位置：不用 outbox 的应用；同一个应用，用裸 sqlx 手写 outbox，使用本 crate 的中间件所取用的那些连接；以及同一个应用，使用本 crate 的 outbox。在最后一个变体中，从处理器之外发布的消息经过 Outbox::wrap。

每次运行使用新的表。 每次运行都重新创建表并填满它，然后排空它。发布场景则改为写入它的行。 在三个循环中，计时窗口都从第一次处理的投递开始，到最后一次结束，因此启动服务和打开连接池都在窗口之外。发布场景的窗口从第一次发布持续到最后一次。每次处理的投递都让一个门闩减一，最后一次计数唤醒这次运行，因此运行无需轮询表或休眠就能知道表已排空。 消息条数来自一次探测，它测量裸循环的速率，因此在任何机器上，测量的运行都至少持续五秒。 各循环交替进行：裸、crate、服务，共三轮。每个循环报告它最佳、中位和最差的一轮。以最佳一轮为准，因为噪声只会让运行变慢。 outbox 运行在 Redis Pub/Sub 上，由一个 worker 供给消息，它最多保留 1024 条未消费的消息，因为订阅的缓冲区装不下时，Pub/Sub 会丢弃消息。 小于任一循环各轮之间波动范围的差异记为 无法区分，从不给出具体数字。往返占一条消息所用时间的至少一半时，该行标为 受数据库限制。这是算出来的。在各轮之前，一次探测在一个连接上为一条服务器作答的语句计时：2000 次 SELECT 1 往返的中位数，与机器信息一起公布。每个场景声明一条消息要付出的往返次数，包括每条语句，以及从连接池取出的每个连接，因为 sqlx 在借出连接前会先 ping 它。往返时间乘以这个次数达到每条消息测得时间的一半时，该行就被标记。

每个单元格在 16 个连接的连接池上排空一张填有 20,000 行的表，分别使用一个、四个和八个 worker，分别使用逐条投递和每批 64 条。PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 采用行锁方式；SQLite 运行在 WAL 模式的本地文件上，采用租约方式，这时一次领取就是一条语句。裸循环在一个连接池上运行 n 个任务，每个任务是一个循环，领取、读取并删除，直到领取返回空。本 crate 的循环在同一个连接池上运行 n 个任务，每个任务是一个读取一个订阅的独立 Broker。服务在一个订阅上以 workers(n) 挂载它的处理器；一个 worker 就是普通的挂载，处理完一次投递后才拉取下一次。三轮交替进行，每个循环取最佳、中位和最差的一轮。

开销图的每个场景都是用户写的服务，构建时不启用 testing 特性，在单线程运行时上启动，连接测试环境的 PostgreSQL，并在旁边统计裸循环。一个生产者在自己的线程和运行时上，在启动和排空之间填充表，因此填充不计入任何一方。outbox 的场景运行在 MemoryBroker 上，同一时间只有一条消息在途。 指令数来自 callgrind，内存分配来自 DHAT。场景先跑一次投递，再跑 1000 次，然后 2000 次。后两者之差就是一条消息的稳态开销，单次投递就是冷启动。运行时等待服务器而挂起期间，计数暂停：那部分工作取决于服务器的时间，而不是代码。 指令数在多次运行之间仍有波动，因为客户端轮询应答时应答是否仍在途中，会改变一条消息要做多少 sqlx 的读取工作。对同一份代码运行五次，一个场景的总数最多波动约 7%，每条消息的数字最多波动约 15%；从不访问数据库的场景，结果精确到每一条指令都一致。与保存的基线对照的运行，在某个场景的指令数多出百分之十时失败。内存分配没有波动：每个场景声明一个上限，即五次完整运行中的最高计数加 0.1%，任何一次运行超过它都会失败。

just bench 这个命令根据 docker-compose.test.yml 启动测试环境，即在主机网络上以 Docker 运行的 PostgreSQL、MySQL 和 Redis，运行每个场景和吞吐量网格，停止测试环境，并重写 docs/benchmarks/results.json。它大约需要半个小时，运行期间机器应专供它使用。RUSTSTREAM_BENCH_SECONDS 设置最短的运行时长，RUSTSTREAM_BENCH_THROUGHPUT_ROWS 设置吞吐量单元格的行数，RUSTSTREAM_BENCH_PAIRS 设置轮数。它会清空 RUSTFLAGS，因此二进制程序不绑定构建它的 CPU。两个命令都按发布版本的方式构建基准测试，启用跨 crate 的 fat 链接时优化，因此这些数字描述的是服务实际交付的代码。 just bench-code 代码计数启动同样的测试环境，需要 valgrind；它会安装锁文件所固定版本的基准测试运行器。just bench-code 5000 让每个场景跑五千次投递，而不是一千次：运行更长，数字更稳定。在 main 上运行 just bench-code --save-baseline=main 记录基线，在分支上运行 just bench-code --baseline=main 与它对照。
ruststream-sqlx 的基准测试数字测量什么，一条消息仍然要付出什么，以及这些数字不能用来得出什么结论。

同一行中的三个循环可以互相比较，因为它们在同一个进程中交替运行，连接同一个数据库。一行不能与其他 Broker crate 公布的行比较：表中的队列在每条消息上做的工作与消息 Broker 不同，它的每条消息都是一次领取、一次结算和一次提交。 在三个循环中，每个数字都包含这些到数据库的往返。在 受数据库限制 的行中，往返至少占一条消息所用时间的一半，因此循环之间的差值是本 crate 和运行时所做工作的下限，而不是对它的测量。大多数 inbox 的行都是 无法区分：本 crate 的工作小于一个等待服务器的循环各轮之间的波动。 outbox 的行测量的是另一件事：跟踪的开销。一条被跟踪的消息在发布前要付出一次插入，在消费者一侧要付出一次取出和一次标记，每一项都是在自己的连接上执行的一条语句。因此按设计，outbox 比不用 outbox 慢好几倍。本 crate 负责的是与手写 outbox 之间的差距，后者执行相同的语句。
documents.s: 与裸 sqlx 循环的对照

documents.t: 只有一个 worker 时，三个循环按同样的顺序做同样的工作。worker 更多时，裸循环运行 n 个领取者，每个领取者是一个独立领取和删除的任务；本 crate 的循环运行 n 个订阅，每个订阅使用自己的 Broker。服务为它的 n 个 worker 运行一个订阅，在 PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 上为每个空闲的 worker 保持一次进行中的领取。因此，本 crate 一列与裸循环一列并排，显示本 crate 在相同并发度下的开销；四个和八个 worker 时本 crate 与服务之间的差距，反映的是一个订阅的领取方式，而不是分发。一个批每次领取最多它的大小那么多行，一次领取服务那么多次投递，因此三个循环的结果很接近。 在 SQLite 上，订阅同一时间只保持一次进行中的领取，因为 SQLite 同一时间只接受一个写入者。裸循环在一个 SQLite 文件上的 n 个领取者，是一个订阅不会采用的形态。四个和八个 worker 时的 SQLite 行显示了这一选择的代价：服务的排空速度只有裸循环的一小部分，也低于它自己一个 worker 时的速度。在 SQLite 上，逐条投递从 workers(n) 中得不到任何好处；批则能获益，批的那几行显示了这一点。

指令计数包括运行时、本 crate，以及 sqlx 驱动程序在服务线程上的工作：为每条语句编码、与服务器交换数据、为每一行解码。旁边裸循环的计数是驱动程序所占的份额，因此两者之差就是本 crate 和运行时。同样的计数在缓存未命中时耗时更多，所以计数不等于时间。 每个数字都是稳态值，即 1000 次投递的运行与 2000 次投递的运行之差。打开连接池的连接、Broker 的启动检查和第一次投递属于冷启动，只付出一次。读指令数时精确到几个百分点即可，不必精确到每一位：与真实服务器通信的服务，在多次运行之间会有波动。

本 crate 遵守整个框架家族的规则：在热路径上，除 sqlx 自身的开销外，每条消息没有内存分配、动态调用、额外的原子操作或复制。仍然存在的开销列在这里，各自注明适用的场合： 读取投递事务 Tx 的处理器，每次投递付出一次引用计数递增；通过 Ctx<keys::Pool> 请求连接池的处理器也付出一次。不使用它们的订阅不付出任何开销。 通过 Repository 或路由的发布，读取 Broker 的关闭标志，即一次原子加载，并唤醒本进程中订阅了该表的订阅，每个订阅一次原子操作。 Routed 查找每条消息的名称，精确名称是一次哈希查找，并对行的 Publish 做一次动态调用。Repository 在编译期确定它的表，两者都不需要。 按名称订阅、而行的事件由服务自己定义时，每条消息付出一次装箱的投递和一次装箱的结算 future。 outbox 通过 OnceLock 读取启动后才设置的连接池，每条被跟踪的消息一次原子加载，并为每条被跟踪消息的 id 消息头文本分配内存。 行锁方式和咨询锁方式为每条处理中的消息或每个处理中的批占用一个池连接：这是持有者终止时由数据库释放的锁的代价。 从处理器之外、通过运行中应用的发布者发布时，每条消息编码进一个单独的缓冲区；裸循环则为所有消息保留一个缓冲区。

测试环境在运行基准测试的机器的主机网络上，以 Docker 运行 PostgreSQL 和 MySQL，不启用持久性：没有 fsync，提交时也不刷新日志。SQLite 运行在 WAL 模式、synchronous = NORMAL 的本地文件上。测量的是一条消息的开销，而不是服务器下面的磁盘。启用持久性的服务要为此付出代价，在每个循环中付出的代价都相同。位于另一台主机上的服务器回答的是关于网络的问题，而不是关于本 crate 的问题。 一行就是一张表、一个小的 JSON 消息体和回环地址上的一台服务器。它测量的是一条消息在本 crate 中的开销，而不是 PostgreSQL、MySQL 或 SQLite 能承载多少。在三个循环中，计时窗口都在最后一次投递被计数时、在它结算之前关闭，因此每次运行都有一次结算在所有循环中都不计入数字。 这些数字是一台机器在某一天的快照，构建信息记录在它们旁边。它们在专供这次运行使用的机器上手动重新测量：它们所显示的差异，比共享机器上的噪声还小。

ruststream-sqlx 所处的位置：在 RustStream 运行时与服务的 sqlx 连接池之间。SQL 为每个订阅构建一次，outbox 可以与任意 Broker 配合。 自上而下依次是服务、RustStream 运行时、本 crate、服务的 sqlx 连接池和数据库挂载到轮询流驱动程序你的服务RustStream 核心ruststream-sqlxsqlx#[subscriber]订阅者处理器RustStream::new(..).with_broker(..)运行时：分发、worker、结算、发布InboxSubscriber领取循环InboxDelivery结算它的行Repository、Routed插入行InboxQueue<Row>描述符SqlxBroker配置Dialect每种数据库的 SQLOutbox中间件，任意 BrokerPool<DB>服务自己的连接池PostgreSQL、MySQL、MariaDB或 SQLite在 testing 特性下，TestApp 在进程内连接：同一个连接池和数据库，使用测试的时钟 以文字阅读本图 你的服务: #[subscriber] 订阅者处理器; RustStream::new(..) .with_broker(..) RustStream 核心: 运行时：分发、worker、结算、发布 ruststream-sqlx: InboxSubscriber 领取循环; InboxDelivery 结算它的行; Repository、Routed 插入行; InboxQueue<Row> 描述符; SqlxBroker 配置; Dialect 每种数据库的 SQL; Outbox 中间件，任意 Broker sqlx: Pool<DB> 服务自己的连接池 #[subscriber] 订阅者处理器 → 运行时：分发、worker、结算、发布: 挂载到 运行时：分发、worker、结算、发布 → InboxSubscriber 领取循环: 轮询流 InboxSubscriber 领取循环 → Pool<DB> 服务自己的连接池 Repository、Routed 插入行 → Pool<DB> 服务自己的连接池 Pool<DB> 服务自己的连接池 → PostgreSQL、MySQL、MariaDB 或 SQLite: 驱动程序 在 testing 特性下，TestApp 在进程内连接： 同一个连接池和数据库，使用测试的时钟 本 crate 在 sqlx 之上实现核心的 Broker trait。它上面的运行时对每个 Broker 都相同。SQL 特有的一切都在本 crate 里：InboxQueue 描述符、领取循环、三种领取方式、每种结果写入什么，以及每种数据库的 SQL。本 crate 支持按描述符和按名称订阅，可以领取批，把行本身交给行模式的处理器，把分区键交给按键分发，向表中发布，并在生成的文档中描述它的服务器。它不提供请求-应答，也不提供事务发布者：事务模式是订阅的一个步骤，处理器通过投递的事务写入数据。 Broker 接收服务的连接池，并且从不关闭它。连接池始终属于服务：它的大小、选项和迁移都由服务决定。SqlxBroker::new 接收一个连接池，而 sqlx 只能在 Tokio 运行时内构建连接池。因此服务在 main 中构建连接池，再把它传给构建应用的函数。

订阅执行的每条语句都由方言构建。PostgreSQL、MySQL 与 MariaDB，以及 SQLite 的方言是内置的。AnyPool 在 Broker 连接时，采用它所连到的那种数据库的方言。对于其他数据库，服务可以提供自己的方言。订阅在打开时根据表的描述构建一次语句。这个描述是一个 const 值，由派生宏或手写的 InboxSpec 生成。因此无论使用派生宏、手写描述还是服务自己的方言，每条消息的开销都相同。随后，启动过程在服务器上预备每条语句，所以缺少表或列时，服务在第一条消息之前就会停止。

重试留在原来的行中。描述符声明由数据库自己移动投递，所以 retry_after 是对该行 retry_after 列的一次 UPDATE，从不发布副本：结算一页用图说明了这一点。发布通过行类型自己的 Publish 实现写入一行。Repository 在编译期确定它的表。Routed 是已连接 Broker 的默认发布者，应答也使用它。它在构建 Broker 时给定的路由中查找消息的名称。两者都以借用切片的形式接收编码后的字节，因此应答的缓冲区在消息之间复用。 每条消息仍然存在的开销由本 crate 列出，并在基准测试中测量： Routed 做一次哈希查找，并对行的 Publish 做一次动态调用。调用产生的 future 原地存放在一个 1024 字节的槽位中，只有更大时才装箱。 一次发布读取 Broker 的关闭标志，即一次原子加载，并唤醒本进程中订阅了该表的订阅，每个订阅一次原子操作。 读取 Tx 或 Ctx<keys::Pool> 的处理器，每次投递付出一次引用计数递增。 按名称订阅、而行的事件由服务自己定义时，每条消息付出一次装箱的投递和一次装箱的结算 future。

在 testing 特性下，TestApp::start 在进程内连接 Broker。连接池以下的部分都不替换：进程内的 Broker 连接测试的连接池所指向的数据库，执行服务的 SQL、表结构和领取方式，并在数据库返回错误的地方返回错误。内存中的 SQLite 可以在没有服务器的情况下服务一个测试。变化的是时间。Broker 从 tokio 时钟读取“现在”，并在连接时以挂钟时间为基准，因此在暂停的时钟上，测试用 tb.advance(..) 推动队列的时间：测试推进过 retry_after 之后，该行就到期了。每次数据库调用都脱离这个时钟运行，所以在数据库的应答尚未返回时，暂停的时钟不会跳到下一个计时器。测试时钟只替代 SystemClock：使用 DatabaseClock 的表读取数据库的时钟，服务自己的时钟也照常生效，与生产环境一样。 测试框架通过 Broker 的计数等待数据库的工作。消息落入测试中某个订阅读取的队列时计一次，重试把行放回队列时再计一次，因此每个到达队列的行都投递并结算之后，tb.settle() 才返回。 各部分如何启动和停止，见生命周期；一行的路径，见路径。

保持一次进行中的领取。与其他领取并行的领取，只在连接池还有空余连接时才开始，订阅占用的连接从不超过连接池大小减一：最后一个连接服务于处理器自己的查询、它们的发布，以及需要连接的结算。连接池空间不足时，同时运行的投递就少一些，共用一个连接池的订阅会彼此留出空间。一次领取什么也没取到之后，订阅每次只领取一次，直到领取再次取到行，因此空表每次等待只看到一次领取，而不是每个 worker 一次。 处理中的投递占用什么，取决于领取方式。在行锁方式和咨询锁方式下，每个投递在结算前都占用一个连接，因此 workers(n) 最多占用 n 个。在租约方式下，领取和结算只在执行语句时占用连接，订阅每隔半个租约取一个连接为租约续约。在事务模式下，无论哪种方式，每个投递都占用它的事务所在的连接。确定连接池大小时，要算上每个占用连接的订阅，再为连接池加一个，以及处理器为自己的查询取用的连接。 有些表同一时间只保持一次进行中的领取，因为并行的领取得不偿失。SQLite 同一时间只接受一个写入者，并发的领取只会互相冲突。在 FIFO 表和带 partition_key 列的表上，两次并发的领取可能不按领取顺序完成。在 MySQL 和 MariaDB 上，租约领取在一个包含多条语句的事务中给行打上租约，这个事务在提交前会锁住它读到的行，包括处理中的租约。worker 仍然并行运行，只是领取轮流进行。 workers_by_key(n) 运行 n 个工作分区，行进入其 partition_key 的哈希所对应的工作分区。同一个键的行绝不会分散到两个工作分区上，因此它们按领取顺序运行。FIFO 组更进一步：在读取它的所有 Broker 和实例之间，一个组同一时间只有一行处于处理中，因为领取只取组的首行，而方言的守卫会锁住这个组。 计算密集的处理器可以用 on_threads(n) 在专用线程上运行。订阅仍然在应用的运行时上领取，每个线程通过自己的一个小连接池查询，未设置时为一个连接。connection_limit 把服务的连接池和每个线程的连接总数限制在数据库允许的范围内：会超出这个限制的订阅不会启动。 服务的两个副本读同一张表时，无需协调就能共享它的行：每个副本各自领取，领取方式保证一行同一时间只在一处。

AND processed_at IS NULL。已经处理过的记录会直接确认投递，不运行处理器，这样被发送两次的副本只处理一次。取出失败时，投递会重试，也不运行处理器。随后由处理器的结果结算记录：确认和 drop 会标记记录，把 processed_at 设为数据库时钟的时间，或者删除该行；retry 和 retry_after 保留记录，记录等待下一次启动。标记失败时会记录日志，保持处理器的结果，同样把记录留给下一次启动。 启动时，在各订阅打开之后，重发过程按名称选出每条未处理的记录，带着它的 id 通过 Broker 的发布者再次发布。重发过程无法读取或发送某条记录时，启动返回错误。两个同时启动的实例可能都发送同一条记录，所以不能重复处理消息的消费者要自己检查这一点。

被跟踪的发布为插入记录单独取一个连接，记录在这个连接上提交。它从不加入投递的事务：事务处理器运行期间写入的记录，无论处理器的结果如何都会提交。因此消息及其记录与服务的业务数据不在同一次提交中。outbox 保证的是一次发布至少投递一次：记录在发送之前写入，每次失败或从未被处理的发送都会留下一条记录，由下一次启动再次发送。常见的事务性 outbox，即业务行和事件行一起提交、由中继轮询该表，在这里就是 inbox 的一张队列表，由一个向另一个 Broker 发布的处理器读取。

注册表是类型系统中的一个列表，每个注册的名称一个节点。因此名称未注册的消息只为每个节点付出一次名称比较，此外没有任何开销：没有内存分配，没有数据库调用，也没有动态调用。被跟踪的发布为插入取一个连接，并为 id 消息头的文本分配内存。被跟踪的投递为取出记录取一个连接，在处理器运行之前归还，以便处理器能发布自己的被跟踪消息，然后为标记再取一个连接。在 #[ruststream::app] 内、注册表构建之后才设置的连接池，通过 OnceLock 读取：每条被跟踪的消息一次原子加载。测试构建默认关闭 outbox，除非设置 RUSTSTREAM_SQLX_OUTBOX=on；生产构建始终跟踪，这个开关在其中被编译掉。 这个模式是事务性 outbox，加上了投递一侧：结束一条记录的是消费者的标记，而不是发送。

领取打开一个事务，用 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED 选出它的行。并发的领取会跳过被锁住的行，而不是等待它们。处理器运行期间事务保持打开，由结算的语句提交它，因此行和它的结果在同一次提交中改变。进程终止时，数据库回滚它的事务，这些行立即到期。代价是每个处理中的投递占用一个连接，并在整个处理器运行期间保持占用。在 MySQL 和 MariaDB 上，除非表指定了隔离级别，事务以 READ COMMITTED 打开，因此领取只锁住它取到的行，而不锁住行之间的间隙。

领取把到期时间写入 locked_until，计入尝试次数并立即提交，因此处理器运行时没有打开的事务，也不占用连接。订阅每隔半个租约为每个处理中的租约续约，所以处理器的运行时间可以超过它的租约。到期时间就是投递的令牌：结算写明它持有的到期时间，只在该行仍持有这个时间时才生效。如果处理器运行期间租约已经到期，原因是续约失败或停止，它会在行中发现另一次领取的令牌，它的结算返回 SqlxBrokerError::LeaseLost。进程终止时，它的行在租约到期后回来：未设置时为三十秒，以整秒计。到期时间由主机计算，因为每次结算都要比较它，所以租约表读取主机的时钟。

领取选出到期的行及其键，在各自的连接上不加等待地尝试获取每个键的锁，跳过被其他会话持有的键，然后在该行仍可领取时取走它。键相同的行逐个进入处理，因此 advisory_lock = "accounts-{account}" 让每个账户的行彼此分开，而其他账户的行照常运行。没有事务保持打开，但持有锁的连接会一直跟随投递，直到它结算。进程终止时，它的会话结束，数据库释放这些锁。键属于数据库，而不属于某张表：键相同的两张表会互相等待。

FOR UPDATE 和咨询锁，MySQL 的加锁读取和锁函数，MariaDB 的 SKIP LOCKED。

数据库 未声明时 表可以声明的级别 PostgreSQL BEGIN，服务器的默认级别 read_committed、repeatable_read、serializable MySQL、MariaDB READ COMMITTED 全部四种 SQLite BEGIN，deferred 模式：deferred、immediate、exclusive 表用 isolation = .. 声明隔离级别，或者在 SQLite 上用 mode = .. 声明模式，本 crate 以此打开行锁方式的领取事务和事务模式的每个事务。PostgreSQL 把 READ UNCOMMITTED 当作 READ COMMITTED 运行，所以它的方言不以这个级别打开事务，声明了它的表在 PostgreSQL Broker 上无法编译。SQLite 以可串行化方式运行每个事务：它的模式决定事务何时获取数据库的写锁，是在第一次写入时，还是在事务开始时。在 SQLite 上，投递的事务一直持有这个锁，直到投递结算，在此期间其他所有写入者都无法进入，领取也包括在内。 MySQL 和 MariaDB 以 READ COMMITTED 打开事务，因为它们的默认级别 REPEATABLE READ 会锁住加锁读取所扫描的行之间的间隙：为处理器保持的领取会阻塞对这张表的每一次插入，直到它结束。在 PostgreSQL 上，repeatable_read 或 serializable 级别的行锁表，在其行的领取和结算同时运行时，领取会返回串行化错误，所以在那里 read_committed 是这种方式实际可用的级别。在 PostgreSQL 上，以这两个级别之一运行事务模式的租约表会在启动时停止：这样的事务看到的是它第一条语句读到的行，看不到续约任务在那之后延长的租约。 本 crate 自己驱动这些事务，而不使用 sqlx 的事务类型：在打开状态下被丢弃的事务会关闭它的连接，由服务器回滚它。这些级别是各数据库自己的：PostgreSQL、MySQL、SQLite。

在 PostgreSQL 上，listen_notify 让其他进程中的订阅也被唤醒。Broker 在 connect 时从连接池取一个连接，在上面监听，一直保留到 shutdown。每个订阅在第一次领取之前监听它的表的通道：通道名就是表名，表有模式时带上模式限定，如 app.jobs。Broker 的每次发布在写入之后，立即在写入该行的连接上执行 SELECT pg_notify(channel, group)；载荷为空的通知唤醒该表的每个订阅。通知失败时会记录日志，发布仍然成功：轮询间隔会让订阅取到这一行。 PostgreSQL 在事务提交时投递通知，因此被唤醒的订阅能看到这一行。监听连接断开期间发出的通知会丢失：Broker 重新连接，并把每个订阅唤醒一次。通道名最多 63 字节，因此对限定名更长的表的订阅会在启动时停止。这个开关在 Broker 的整个生命周期内占用一个连接，并让每次发布多执行一条语句。发出通知的事务在提交时还会获取一个服务器全局的锁，因此发出通知的提交依次执行，这会限制大量并发的写入者。在其他数据库上，listen_notify 无法编译。 服务器在 NOTIFY 一页说明了这个机制：在提交时投递，载荷小于 8000 字节，以及标识符的 63 字节限制。提交时的锁由 PostgreSQL 开发者在邮件列表中说明。

The parts of ruststream-sqlx a service uses, one page per component: the inbox broker SqlxBroker, the queue tables it serves, the messages and headers a row hands its handler, the subscriptions and the forms they claim rows in, settlement, transactions, the context and time of a delivery, publishing and waking a subscription, the databases, the AsyncAPI document, the tests, and the transactional outbox. The crate has two halves. The inbox keeps a task queue in a table of the service's own database: a subscription claims rows, a handler's outcome settles them, and a publish writes a row through the service's own SQL. A task can then commit in the same transaction as the data it serves. The outbox is a plugin over any RustStream broker: it records what a service publishes in a table of its own until a consumer has processed it, and publishes again at startup what was not processed. The outbox needs no inbox, and a service may use both. Every feature is off by default and only adds to the crate. inbox turns the broker on and outbox the outbox. postgres, mysql (MySQL and MariaDB) and sqlite each add a built-in dialect and its sqlx driver. any serves an AnyPool, chrono or time the time columns, and json a headers column of JSON. testing adds the in-process mode a TestApp test connects, and the outbox's test switch. asyncapi adds the table a subscription reads to the generated document. any, chrono, time and asyncapi turn inbox on with them. Beside the core's required traits, the broker serves batches of rows (BatchSubscriber) and lends a handler in row mode the row itself (Carries and CarriesBatch). Its default publisher is the route table, Routed, so a reply or an Out slot without a policy of its own writes a row through a route.

With the asyncapi feature the document names the database server and, on each subscription's channel, the table it reads and its group; rows get their schema. The core builds the AsyncAPI document from the app, before anything connects. This crate adds what it knows about the parts the core describes. A server reports the database the pool reaches: its host and port and the protocol, never a credential. A channel of an InboxQueue subscription reports the table it reads under the extension x-sqlx, with the group its name selects. Everything comes from the service's own declarations: the pool's options, the table's description and the subscription's name. A message a handler decodes is documented by its type's JsonSchema, as on every broker. A handler in row mode takes the row itself, so the row's JsonSchema documents the message: the derive names schemars through the core, #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")]. A pool built with connect_lazy builds the document with no database in reach, inside a Tokio runtime.

The dependency line: ruststream-sqlx = { version = "0.7", features = ["inbox", "postgres", "asyncapi"] } The service registers its broker under the label postgres, the key of its server in the document. The tests build the document with build_spec and read it as JSON. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_asyncapi.rs fn service(pool: PgPool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("office", "0.1.0")).with_broker_labeled( "postgres", SqlxBroker::new(pool), |b| { b.include(send_email); b.include(render); b.include(send_mail); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = pool(&env::var("DATABASE_URL")?)?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) } examples/manual/sqlx_asyncapi.rs fn service(pool: PgPool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("office", "0.1.0")).with_broker_labeled( "postgres", SqlxBroker::new(pool), |b| { let email = subscriber("emails", Mailer).map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<SendEmail>::new("emails")); b.include(email.build()); let report = subscriber("reports", Renderer) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<RenderReport>::new("reports")); b.include(report.build()); let mail = subscriber("mail", Postman).map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<Mail>::new("mail")); b.include(mail.build()); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = pool(&env::var("DATABASE_URL")?)?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) } The mail handler takes the row of mail_jobs itself, and the message it reads is documented by the row's columns. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_asyncapi.rs /// A mail the handler takes as the row itself: its `JsonSchema` documents the message. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Inbox, sqlx::FromRow, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] #[inbox(table = "mail_jobs")] struct Mail { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(group)] name: String, recipient: String, subject: Option<String>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<Mail>::new("mail"))] async fn send_mail(mail: &Mail) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(to = %mail.recipient, subject = ?mail.subject, "mailing"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/sqlx_asyncapi.rs use ruststream::runtime::SoloCarried; /// A mail the handler takes as the row itself: its `JsonSchema` documents the message. #[derive(Debug, Clone, sqlx::FromRow, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Mail { id: i64, recipient: String, subject: Option<String>, } impl InboxTable for Mail { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<()>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("mail_jobs", Column::new("id").generated()) .group(Column::new("name")) .data(&[Column::new("recipient"), Column::new("subject")]); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } // Row mode: a handler takes the row itself. impl Input for Mail { type Axis = SoloCarried<Self>; } struct Postman; impl Handle<Mail> for Postman { fn handle( &self, mail: &Mail, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(to = %mail.recipient, subject = ?mail.subject, "mailing"); ready(Ok(())) } }

Each InboxQueue channel carries x-sqlx: the table it reads, qualified with its schema, and the group its name selects where the table has groups. The extension holds two fields. table is the table's name, with its schema in front where the description names one (app.email_jobs). group is the subscription's name, present only when the table has a group column: in a table without groups the name addresses the whole table. A channel the service publishes to and a subscription by name carry no extension: a name leads into a table through a route, which the channel does not describe.

The channel emails reports { "table": "app.email_jobs", "group": "emails" }, and the channel reports reports { "table": "reports" }. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_asyncapi.rs /// One row of `app.email_jobs`: the channel of each subscription names the table and its group. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "email_jobs", schema = "app")] struct SendEmail { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(group)] name: String, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } /// One row of `reports`, a table without groups: its channel names the table alone. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "reports")] struct RenderReport { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<SendEmail>::new("emails"))] async fn send_email(email: &Email) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(to = %email.to, "sending"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<RenderReport>::new("reports"))] async fn render(report: &Report) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(month = report.month, "rendering"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/sqlx_asyncapi.rs use ruststream_sqlx::dialect::Column; use ruststream_sqlx::spec::Payload; use ruststream_sqlx::{InboxSpec, InboxTable}; /// One row of `app.email_jobs`: the channel of each subscription names the table and its group. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct SendEmail { id: i64, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for SendEmail { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<(Payload,)>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("email_jobs", Column::new("id").generated()) .within("app") .group(Column::new("name")) .payload(Column::new("payload")); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl PayloadRow for SendEmail { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } /// One row of `reports`, a table without groups: its channel names the table alone. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct RenderReport { id: i64, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for RenderReport { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<(Payload,)>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("reports", Column::new("id").generated()).payload(Column::new("payload")); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl PayloadRow for RenderReport { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } struct Mailer; impl Handle<Email> for Mailer { fn handle( &self, email: &Email, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(to = %email.to, "sending"); ready(Ok(())) } } struct Renderer; impl Handle<Report> for Renderer { fn handle( &self, report: &Report, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(month = report.month, "rendering"); ready(Ok(())) } }

The server is the pool's host and port with the protocol postgres or mysql, SQLite in process with no host, an AnyPool by its scheme, never a credential. A broker registered with with_broker_labeled is a server of the document, under its label. On Postgres, MySQL and MariaDB the server is read off the pool's connect options: the host is the host and port, and the protocol is postgres or mysql. The user, the password and the database name stay out of it. SQLite runs inside the service, so its server names the protocol sqlite and no host: neither the file's path nor any other part of the URL reaches the document. An AnyPool is described by the scheme of its URL, as the broker of that database describes itself. The document is published and shared, so a password in the pool's URL stays in the pool.

The pool comes from the URL a deployment configures, password included; the document's server is db.internal:5432 with the protocol postgres. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_asyncapi.rs /// The pool on the database a deployment configures; it connects on first use. fn pool(url: &str) -> Result<PgPool, sqlx::Error> { PgPoolOptions::new().max_connections(8).connect_lazy(url) } examples/manual/sqlx_asyncapi.rs /// The pool on the database a deployment configures; it connects on first use. fn pool(url: &str) -> Result<PgPool, sqlx::Error> { PgPoolOptions::new().max_connections(8).connect_lazy(url) }

SqlxBroker serves the queues in the tables of the service's sqlx pool; new records the pool, and connect checks one connection and picks the dialect. SqlxBroker::new takes a Pool<DB> of a database a built-in dialect serves: Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB or SQLite. It does no I/O, and the broker never closes the pool: the pool stays the service's. sqlx builds a pool only inside a Tokio runtime, so a service on the inbox builds its pool in #[tokio::main] and hands it to the function that builds the app. The settings that follow new are builder steps: routes that lead publishes into tables, the poll interval and the lease every subscription takes unless it names its own, and the connection limit of dedicated threads. At startup the runtime connects the broker and receives a ConnectedSqlxBroker. The connect takes one connection from the pool, so a database out of reach fails startup with SqlxBrokerError::Connect. It also picks the dialect from that connection, which matters for an AnyPool. Every subscription then reads one queue through an InboxQueue descriptor, and the startup checks run as it opens. At shutdown the runtime turns the connected broker into a ClosedSqlxBroker. A message in work holds connections of the pool by the form its table claims rows in, and a publish takes one more; Connections shows how to size the pool.

The service serves the queue thumbnails from a SQLite file: main builds the pool, creates the table and runs the app. cargo run -p ruststream-sqlx --example sqlx_broker --features inbox,sqlite,chrono,testing starts it. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::SqlitePool; /// One row of `thumbnail_jobs`, claimed under a lease. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "thumbnail_jobs")] struct MakeThumbnail { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<MakeThumbnail>::new("thumbnails"))] async fn thumbnail(image: &Image) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(path = %image.path, "making a thumbnail"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("thumbnails", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<MakeThumbnail>("thumbnails"), |b| { b.include(thumbnail); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = SqlitePool::connect("sqlite:thumbnails.db?mode=rwc").await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) } examples/manual/sqlx_broker.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::SqlitePool; /// One row of `thumbnail_jobs`, claimed under a lease. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct MakeThumbnail { id: i64, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for MakeThumbnail { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<(Lease<DateTime<Utc>>, Payload)>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("thumbnail_jobs", Column::new("id").generated()) .lease(Column::new("locked_until")) .payload(Column::new("payload")); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl PayloadRow for MakeThumbnail { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } struct Thumbnail; impl Handle<Image> for Thumbnail { fn handle( &self, image: &Image, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(path = %image.path, "making a thumbnail"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("thumbnails", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<MakeThumbnail>("thumbnails"), |b| { let thumbnail = subscriber("thumbnails", Thumbnail) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<MakeThumbnail>::new("thumbnails")); b.include(thumbnail.build()); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = SqlitePool::connect("sqlite:thumbnails.db?mode=rwc").await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) }

Each message in work holds pool connections by its form; workers(n) claims in parallel but always leaves the pool one connection for handlers. A subscription mounted with workers(n) keeps a claim in flight for each free worker. It never holds more than the pool's size less one connection, so the pool always keeps one for the handlers' own queries, their publishes and the settlements that take one. A second claim starts only while the pool has a connection to spare, so subscriptions that share a pool leave each other room, and a pool short of room runs fewer deliveries at once. A subscription keeps one claim in flight on SQLite, which takes one writer at a time, on a table whose groups keep their order, and with a partition_key column under workers_by_key(n). What a delivery holds depends on the form: Form Connections row lock one per delivery in work and one per claim in flight, for the whole handler lease one for each claim's and each settlement's statement, and one per subscription each half lease to extend the leases advisory lock one per delivery in work until it settles, in a batch too transactional mode, any form one per delivery in work, for the transaction its handler writes through A publish takes a connection of its own for its insert, and a handler that reads keys::Pool takes one for each query. So a pool is sized for every subscription: n for each workers(n), one more for the pool, and the connections the handlers take for their own work. In the lease form a pool of n + 1 lets every free worker claim at once. Under sqlx's default test_before_acquire, each acquire pings the connection first, a round trip a pool built with test_before_acquire(false) skips. Subscriptions on dedicated threads open connections of their own on top of the pool.

Four workers resize images, and each handler records its image through the pool; the pool has room for the four workers, the connection the subscription leaves free and the handlers' writes. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker_connections.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::Sqlite; #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "resize_jobs")] struct ResizeImage { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } // The handler takes a connection of the pool for its own write. #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<ResizeImage>::new("resizes"))] async fn resize(image: &Image, Ctx(pool): Ctx<keys::Pool<Sqlite>>) -> HandlerOutcome { let recorded = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO resized (path) VALUES (?)") .bind(&image.path) .execute(&pool) .await; match recorded { Ok(_) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(error) => { tracing::warn!(subscription = "resizes", path = %image.path, %error, "not recorded"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("resizer", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<ResizeImage>("resizes"), |b| { b.include(resize.workers(nonzero!(4))); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { // Four workers, one connection the subscription always leaves free, and one for the // handlers' own writes and the publishes. let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new() .max_connections(6) .connect("sqlite:resizes.db?mode=rwc") .await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) } examples/manual/sqlx_broker_connections.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::Sqlite; struct Resize; // The handler takes a connection of the pool for its own write. impl Handle<Image, (), (), PoolContext<Sqlite>> for Resize { async fn handle( &self, image: &Image, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, PoolContext<Sqlite>>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Ok(Ctx(pool)) = Ctx::<keys::Pool<Sqlite>>::from_context(ctx).await; let recorded = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO resized (path) VALUES (?)") .bind(&image.path) .execute(&pool) .await; recorded.map(drop).map_err(|error| { tracing::warn!(subscription = "resizes", path = %image.path, %error, "not recorded"); HandlerOutcome::retry() }) } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("resizer", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<ResizeImage>("resizes"), |b| { let resize = subscriber("resizes", Resize) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<ResizeImage>::new("resizes")) .workers(nonzero!(4)); b.include(resize.build()); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { // Four workers, one connection the subscription always leaves free, and one for the // handlers' own writes and the publishes. let pool = SqlitePoolOptions::new() .max_connections(6) .connect("sqlite:resizes.db?mode=rwc") .await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) }

SqlxBrokerError is the inbox's one error type: connecting, statements, the schema, declarations, leases, transactions, publishes, and a closed broker. Every variant about a subscription names the subscription, the table and the row type, so one line of a log says where to look. The database's own error is its source. Variant When Connect the connect could not take a connection from the pool Backend an AnyPool reached a database whose dialect's feature is off Schema a statement failed to prepare at startup: the table lacks a table or a column the description names Dialect the dialect could not build a statement for the table ServerTooOld the server is older than the statements of the table's form need Declaration the mount declared what the table cannot carry ConnectionLimit a subscription on dedicated threads would pass the broker's connection limit AlreadySubscribed a second subscription to one queue on the same broker Sqlx a statement failed while the subscription ran BatchRolledBack an earlier settlement of a batch failed, so the batch rolls back LeaseLost in the lease form, the lease ran out and another claim took the row, so the settlement took no effect TransactionHeld in transactional mode, the handler kept its transaction past its return Listen listen_notify could not listen on the table's channel Publish the service's Publish failed Header the publish carries a header the table cannot hold byte for byte NoRoute no route leads the name to a table Closed the broker was shut down, and a handle outlived it A service meets the error in three places. A failed startup carries it as the source of the runtime's error, and the service exits before it reads a row. A publish from a handler returns it inside the core's PublishError, and the handler decides how its delivery settles. A settlement that fails, such as LeaseLost, goes to the log with the row's id. The enum is #[non_exhaustive], so a match on it ends with a wildcard arm.

An invoice the database refuses to write is logged with its cause, and the payment waits a minute before it is billed again. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker_errors.rs #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<PaymentJob>::new("payments"))] async fn bill(payment: &Payment, Out(invoices): Out<impl Publisher, Invoices>) -> HandlerOutcome { let invoice = Invoice { payment: payment.id, }; if let Err(error) = invoices.message(&invoice).publish().await { // The error names the destination, the table and the database's reason. tracing::warn!(subscription = "payments", payment.id, %error, "invoice not written"); return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(60)); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/sqlx_broker_errors.rs struct Bill; impl<Entry> Handle<Payment, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Bill where Entry: OutEntry<Invoices, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let invoice = Invoice { payment: payment.id, }; outs.get(Invoices) .message(&invoice) .publish() .await .map_err(|error| { // The error names the destination, the table and the database's reason. tracing::warn!(subscription = "payments", payment.id, %error, "invoice not written"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(60)) }) } }

One glob, ruststream_sqlx::prelude, brings the core prelude, the derives, the broker, InboxQueue, its steps, the publish policies and the keys. use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; is the one import a service on the inbox writes. It carries the core's own prelude, so #[subscriber], RustStream, HandlerOutcome and Out come with it. It adds the derives Inbox and InboxHeaders, the broker SqlxBroker, the descriptor InboxQueue, the mount steps of InboxSettings and InboxThreads, the traits Insert and Publish, the publish policies Repository and Routed, and the keys a handler reads. Publish here is the trait a table implements to receive a publish, not a policy. Another broker's prelude may name its publish policy Publish, so a file that imports both globs names one of them by its path. The rest is imported by path: the event traits such as Ack and Fetch, DatabaseClock, HeaderColumn, the dialect and spec modules a table described by hand uses, and everything of the outbox.

The descriptor with its poll interval, the attempt key, the derive, the routes and the Routed policy of an Out slot all come from the one glob. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "order_jobs")] struct OrderJob { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(attempt, generated)] attempt: i16, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Receipt)] struct Receipts; #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<OrderJob>::new("orders").poll_interval(Duration::from_millis(200)))] async fn confirm( order: &Order, Out(receipts): Out<impl Publisher, Receipts>, Ctx(attempt): Ctx<keys::Attempt>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, ?attempt, "confirming"); match receipts .message(&Receipt { order: order.id }) .publish() .await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(error) => { tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, %error, "no receipt"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { let broker = SqlxBroker::new(pool) .route::<OrderJob>("orders") .route::<ReceiptJob>("receipts"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(confirm).out(Receipts, Routed).build(); }) } examples/manual/sqlx_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; /// The slot receipts leave through. struct Receipts; impl OutSlot for Receipts { const NAME: &'static str = "Receipts"; // `Receipt` fixes its destination, so no transform on this slot may name one. type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Receipts> for Receipt {} struct Confirm; impl<Entry> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Entry,)>, InboxContext> for Confirm where Entry: OutEntry<Receipts, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, ctx: &mut Context<'_, InboxContext>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Ok(Ctx(attempt)) = Ctx::<keys::Attempt>::from_context(ctx).await; tracing::info!(order.id, ?attempt, "confirming"); let receipt = Receipt { order: order.id }; outs.get(Receipts) .message(&receipt) .publish() .await .map_err(|error| { tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, %error, "no receipt"); HandlerOutcome::retry() }) } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { let broker = SqlxBroker::new(pool) .route::<OrderJob>("orders") .route::<ReceiptJob>("receipts"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let confirm = subscriber("orders", Confirm).map_source(|_| { InboxQueue::<OrderJob>::new("orders").poll_interval(Duration::from_millis(200)) }); b.include(confirm.build()).out(Receipts, Routed).build(); }) }

Shutdown returns ClosedSqlxBroker, releases every advisory lock in work, and a publisher kept past it reports SqlxBrokerError::Closed. At shutdown the runtime first stops the subscriptions and lets the handlers in work finish, up to its shutdown timeout. Then it shuts the broker down: the claim loops stop, and so does the extension of the leases. A delivery in work in the lease form keeps its lease, which runs out unless the delivery settles first; its row then returns to the queue. In the advisory lock form the broker releases the lock of every delivery in work and waits for the settlements in flight, so no lock of the broker is left. The pool stays open: the broker never closes it. The service closes it after run returns, once nothing of the app uses it. A handle taken before shutdown, such as a repository publisher, refuses every publish afterwards with SqlxBrokerError::Closed, and never writes a row past the shutdown. A tool that drives the broker by hand receives the ClosedSqlxBroker, whose locks_released and connections_closed count what the shutdown did to the advisory locks.

run returns once the handlers have drained and the broker has shut down, and the service then closes its pool. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker_shutdown.rs fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("exports", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<Export>("exports"), |b| { b.include(export); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = SqlitePool::connect("sqlite:exports.db?mode=rwc").await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; // `run` returns once the handlers have drained and the broker has shut down; the pool is // still open, and closing it is the service's call. service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) } examples/manual/sqlx_broker_shutdown.rs fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("exports", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<Export>("exports"), |b| { let export = subscriber("exports", Exporter) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<Export>::new("exports")); b.include(export.build()); }, ) } #[tokio::main] async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let pool = SqlitePool::connect("sqlite:exports.db?mode=rwc").await?; sqlx::raw_sql(SCHEMA).execute(&pool).await?; // `run` returns once the handlers have drained and the broker has shut down; the pool is // still open, and closing it is the service's call. service(pool.clone()).run().await?; pool.close().await; Ok(()) }

A subscription builds and prepares its statements when it opens, so a missing table or column, a retry the table cannot carry or a second reader stops startup. A struct that cannot drive a queue does not compile at all; the derive lists those errors. What only the database can tell is checked at startup. Each subscription builds its statements with the broker's dialect and prepares each one on the server. A table or a column the description names and the database lacks fails startup with SqlxBrokerError::Schema, which names the subscription, the table and the statement. Preparing checks names, not column types: a row whose columns do not decode reaches the decode policy instead. The other refusals at startup: Error When Declaration the mount declares what the table cannot carry: max_attempts(n) without dead_letter(..) or the reverse, a cap on a table without an attempt column, or transactional mode in the lease form at a strict isolation level on Postgres Dialect the dialect cannot build a statement the table needs ServerTooOld a MySQL older than 8.0.1 or a MariaDB older than 10.6, which lack SKIP LOCKED AlreadySubscribed a second subscription to one queue on the same broker; a table without a group column is one queue Connect, Backend the broker could not take a connection, or an AnyPool reached a database whose dialect feature is off The service runs its migrations before the app starts, and the checks then see the schema the release reads.

A release adds an attempt column to the queue; main applies the schema before the app starts, and a table without the column stops startup with SqlxBrokerError::Schema. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_broker_startup.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::SqlitePool; #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "invoice_jobs")] struct SendInvoice { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, // The column this release adds; A handler reads the inbox's context through Ctx<keys::..>: the transaction, the pool and the attempt, in that order, leaving out what it does not need. The keys module holds three keys, each read as a handler parameter: Key Value What it is keys::Tx<DB> Tx<DB> the delivery's transaction, in transactional mode keys::Pool<DB> Pool<DB> the service's pool, whose writes commit on their own keys::Attempt Option<u64> the delivery's attempt, 1 for the first, None where the table counts none A handler's first Ctx names the context the delivery builds for it, and decides which keys compile after it. After keys::Tx come the other two, after keys::Pool only keys::Attempt, and nothing after keys::Attempt. So the order Tx, Pool, Attempt fits every handler, with the keys it does not need left out, and a key in another place does not compile. A key's type names its database, as in keys::Pool<Sqlite>. A delivery builds the context only for a handler that reads it: a pool handle and the attempt are copied, and the transaction is lent. The framework's extractors stand beside these keys: Headers<T>, State<T>, and a &mut Context parameter whose headers() read the delivery's headers. In the manual form the body resolves a key with Ctx::<keys::Attempt>::from_context(ctx), its Handle impl naming the context: keys::InboxContext for the attempt, keys::PoolContext<DB> after the pool, keys::TxContext<DB> after the transaction.

A transactional signup handler logs every attempt through the pool and opens the account through the delivery's transaction; a retry keeps the log and discards the account. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_context.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; /// One row of `signup_jobs`. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "signup_jobs")] struct OpenAccount { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(attempt, generated)] attempt: i16, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<OpenAccount>::new("signups"))] async fn open_account( signup: &Signup, Ctx(mut tx): Ctx<keys::Tx<Sqlite>>, Ctx(pool): Ctx<keys::Pool<Sqlite>>, Ctx(attempt): Ctx<keys::Attempt>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { // Through the pool: the line stays whatever the outcome. It comes first, because on SQLite // the delivery's transaction holds the database's write lock from its first write. let _ = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO signup_log (email, attempt) VALUES (?, ?)") .bind(&signup.email) .bind(attempt.and_then(|attempt| i64::try_from(attempt).ok())) .execute(&pool) .await; // Through the transaction: the account commits with the acknowledgement, or not at all. let opened = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO accounts (email) VALUES (?)") .bind(&signup.email) .execute(&mut *tx) .await; if opened.is_err() || !register(signup, attempt).await { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("accounts", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<OpenAccount>("signups"), |b| { b.include(open_account.transactional()); }, ) } examples/manual/sqlx_context.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; /// One row of `signup_jobs`. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct OpenAccount { id: i64, attempt: i16, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for OpenAccount { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<(Attempt, Lease<DateTime<Utc>>, Payload)>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("signup_jobs", Column::new("id").generated()) .attempt(Column::new("attempt").generated()) .lease(Column::new("locked_until")) .payload(Column::new("payload")); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl AttemptRow for OpenAccount { type Attempt = i16; fn attempt(&self) -> &i16 { &self.attempt } } impl PayloadRow for OpenAccount { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } struct OpenAccountHandler; impl Handle<Signup, (), (), TxContext<Sqlite>> for OpenAccountHandler { async fn handle( &self, signup: &Signup, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, TxContext<Sqlite>>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Ctx(mut tx) = Ctx::<keys::Tx<Sqlite>>::from_context(ctx).await?; let Ctx(pool) = Ctx::<keys::Pool<Sqlite>>::from_context(ctx).await?; let Ctx(attempt) = Ctx::<keys::Attempt>::from_context(ctx).await?; // Through the pool: the line stays whatever the outcome. It comes first, because on // SQLite the delivery's transaction holds the database's write lock from its first write. let _ = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO signup_log (email, attempt) VALUES (?, ?)") .bind(&signup.email) .bind(attempt.and_then(|attempt| i64::try_from(attempt).ok())) .execute(&pool) .await; // Through the transaction: the account commits with the acknowledgement, or not at all. let opened = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO accounts (email) VALUES (?)") .bind(&signup.email) .execute(&mut *tx) .await; if opened.is_err() || !register(signup, attempt).await { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("accounts", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<OpenAccount>("signups"), |b| { let open_account = subscriber("signups", OpenAccountHandler) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<OpenAccount>::new("signups")) .transactional(); b.include(open_account.build()); }, ) }

keys::Attempt reads the delivery's attempt, 1 for the first: the attempt column as it stood before the claim, None where the table has none. A #[field(attempt)] column counts the deliveries of a row, so it starts at 1, usually as the column's default. A retry counts the attempt in the row lock form; the claim counts it in the lease and advisory lock forms, so a crash with the row in work spends one too. Either way a delivery reports the attempt as it stood before its claim, and the first delivery reads 1 in every form. The field is an i16, i32, i64, u16, u32 or u64 (AttemptColumn), and a negative value reads as 0. A column of another type converts into the field through #[sqlx(try_from = "..")], by hand through .attempt_from::<T>(..). A row that does not decode still reports its attempt, read alone, so a retry cap counts it. The backoff is the handler's: it reads the attempt and answers with retry_after of the delay it wants. By hand, .attempt(..) names the column, Attempt goes into the description's type, and the row reads its attempt through AttemptRow.

A supplier's API answers from the third attempt on, and the handler waits twice as long before each new one: one second, then two. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_context_attempt.rs use std::time::Duration; use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::SqlitePool; /// One row of `stock_jobs`: `attempt` counts the deliveries, 1 for the first. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "stock_jobs")] struct SyncStock { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(attempt, generated)] attempt: i16, #[field(retry_after)] retry_after: DateTime<Utc>, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<SyncStock>::new("stock"))] async fn sync(item: &Item, Ctx(attempt): Ctx<keys::Attempt>) -> HandlerOutcome { let attempt = attempt.unwrap_or(1); if fetch_level(item, attempt).await { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } // Doubling backoff: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, ... let exponent = u32::try_from(attempt.min(16)).unwrap_or(16); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(1 << (exponent - 1))) } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("stock", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<SyncStock>("stock"), |b| { b.include(sync); }, ) } examples/manual/sqlx_context_attempt.rs use std::time::Duration; use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::SqlitePool; /// One row of `stock_jobs`: `attempt` counts the deliveries, 1 for the first. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct SyncStock { id: i64, attempt: i16, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for SyncStock { type Id = i64; type Table = InboxSpec<( Attempt, RetryAfter<DateTime<Utc>>, Lease<DateTime<Utc>>, Payload, )>; const TABLE: Self::Table = InboxSpec::new("stock_jobs", Column::new("id").generated()) .attempt(Column::new("attempt").generated()) .retry_after(Column::new("retry_after")) .lease(Column::new("locked_until")) .payload(Column::new("payload")); fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl AttemptRow for SyncStock { type Attempt = i16; fn attempt(&self) -> &i16 { &self.attempt } } impl PayloadRow for SyncStock { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } struct FetchLevel; impl Handle<Item, (), (), InboxContext> for FetchLevel { async fn handle( &self, item: &Item, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, InboxContext>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Ctx(attempt) = Ctx::<keys::Attempt>::from_context(ctx).await?; let attempt = attempt.unwrap_or(1); if fetch_level(item, attempt).await { return Ok(()); } // Doubling backoff: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, ... let exponent = u32::try_from(attempt.min(16)).unwrap_or(16); Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs( 1 << (exponent - 1), ))) } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("stock", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<SyncStock>("stock"), |b| { let sync = subscriber("stock", FetchLevel) .map_source(|_| InboxQueue::<SyncStock>::new("stock")); b.include(sync.build()); }, ) }

keys::Pool gives a handler the service's pool, whose writes commit on their own whatever the outcome; on dedicated threads it is the thread's pool. Ctx(pool): Ctx<keys::Pool<Sqlite>> binds a Pool<Sqlite>, a handle the read clones; every delivery of an InboxQueue subscription lends it. A write through it commits on its own: a retry, a drop or a rolled-back transaction leaves it in place. That makes it the place for what must outlive the outcome: a delivery log, an error note, a counter. Each query takes a connection of the pool for its run, on top of the ones the subscription holds, so the pool is sized for the handlers' own queries too (Connections). On SQLite a delivery's transaction holds the database's write lock from its first write, so a transactional handler writes through the pool before it writes through tx. On dedicated threads the key yields the thread's own pool, built from the service pool's options, whose connections open on the thread and close with it. After keys::Tx the key still reads the pool, and keys::Attempt may follow it (Context).

Every attempt to send a text message writes a line to the delivery log through the pool, and the line stays when the gateway is busy and the handler retries. Macros Manual examples/sqlx_context_pool.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; /// One row of `sms_jobs`. #[derive(Inbox, sqlx::FromRow)] #[inbox(table = "sms_jobs")] struct SendSms { #[field(id, generated)] id: i64, #[field(attempt, generated)] attempt: i16, #[field(locked_until)] locked_until: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, #[field(payload)] payload: Vec<u8>, } #[subscriber(InboxQueue::<SendSms>::new("sms"))] async fn send( sms: &Sms, Ctx(pool): Ctx<keys::Pool<Sqlite>>, Ctx(attempt): Ctx<keys::Attempt>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let sent = deliver(sms, attempt).await; // The line commits on its own: a retry leaves it in place. let _ = sqlx::query("INSERT INTO delivery_log (phone, sent) VALUES (?, ?)") .bind(&sms.phone) .bind(sent) .execute(&pool) .await; if sent { HandlerOutcome::ack() } else { HandlerOutcome::retry() } } fn service(pool: SqlitePool) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("sms", "0.1.0")).with_broker( SqlxBroker::new(pool).route::<SendSms>("sms"), |b| { b.include(send); }, ) } examples/manual/sqlx_context_pool.rs use ruststream_sqlx::prelude::*; use sqlx::{Sqlite, SqlitePool}; /// One row of `sms_jobs`. #[derive(sqlx::FromRow)] struct SendSms { id: i64, attempt: i16, payload: Vec<u8>, } impl InboxTable for SendSms { type Id = i64; fn id(&self) -> &i64 { &self.id } } impl AttemptRow for SendSms { type Attempt = i16; fn attempt(&self) -> &i16 { &self.attempt } } impl PayloadRow for SendSms { type Column = Vec<u8>; fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.payload } } struct SendText;
